🔐 OAuth Login Setup Wizard

Kakao and Google login for a Flutter app — from console setup to a CI/CD build that just works

projectops GitHub → | |

⏱️ Estimated time 20–40 min · 📑 7–10 steps (depends on what you pick) · 🎒 You need a Flutter project · a Kakao Developers and/or Google (Firebase) account · Python 3
🎁 When done, you get native config applied by one command, Dart login code, the GitHub Secrets to register and the exact CI/CD steps · 📖 Read the full guide →

Your progress is saved in this browser automatically. Close the window and reopen it to pick up where you left off.

Which login do you want?

🎯 Goal of this step: pick the providers. The wizard then shows only the steps you need. You can come back and change this later.

How this wizard works

  1. Collect your app IDs and signing-key fingerprints (both providers need them)
  2. Register the app in each provider's console, following the steps line by line
  3. Get the GitHub Secrets, the CI/CD steps and the .gitignore lines
  4. Run one command that patches AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist for you

 Android signing-key fingerprints

            

                🎯 Goal of this step: collect the SHA-1 of every key that signs your Android builds. Google needs the SHA-1, Kakao needs a "key hash" made from it. A build signed with an unregistered key fails to log in — this is the most common OAuth breakage.
            


            
Which key signs which build

            

                

                    
                        

                            Build
                            Signed with
                        

                    
                    
                        

                            flutter run on your computer
                            Debug key ~/.android/debug.keystore (different on every computer)
                        

                        

                            Test APK (@projectops apk build → ANDROID-TEST-APK) and Firebase App Distribution (ANDROID-FIREBASE-CICD)
                            Upload key from the RELEASE_KEYSTORE_BASE64 secret
                        

                        

                            App installed from Google Play (ANDROID-PLAYSTORE-CICD)
                            Play App Signing key — Google re-signs the app, so this SHA-1 is different from your upload key
                        

                        

                            Self-hosted APK (ANDROID-SELFHOSTED-CICD)
                            The DEBUG_KEYSTORE secret, unless the repository variable ANDROID_SELFHOSTED_RELEASE_SIGNING=true switches it to the upload key
                        

                    
                

            


            

                
Get the SHA-1 (copy the line that starts with SHA1:)

                

                    
                    
                

                
1) Debug key (no password needed)

                

                
                
2) Upload (release) key — asks for the keystore password. Replace YOUR_KEY_ALIAS; the Play Store wizard puts the keystore at android/app/keystore/key.jks

                

                
                
Or let the wizard CLI print SHA-1, SHA-256 and the Kakao key hash at once (debug key by default)

                

                
                
keytool not found? It ships with Android Studio: /Applications/Android Studio.app/Contents/jbr/Contents/Home/bin/keytool (macOS) or C:\Program Files\Android\Android Studio\jbr\bin\keytool.exe (Windows).

                
3) Play App Signing key: Google Play Console → your app → the App signing page (under App integrity) → "App signing key certificate" → SHA-1. Only exists after the app is set up in Play Console.

            


            

                

                    
                    
                    

                

                

                    
                    
                    

                

                

                    
                    
                    

                

            

            
The Kakao key hash under each field is computed in this browser from the SHA-1 (same result as keytool -exportcert … | openssl sha1 -binary | openssl base64).

 Google Sign-In setup

            

                🎯 Goal of this step: create the OAuth clients (Android, iOS, Web) and copy the iOS client ID and the Web client ID (used as serverClientId).
            


            
Where do you set it up?

            

                
                
                
            


            

                

                    Open Firebase console
                    
    
                        
  1. Project settings → Your apps → add an Android app with the package name below
    2. 
                        
  2. On that Android app, Add fingerprint for every SHA-1 below (SHA-256 is optional)
    3. 
                        
  3. Add an iOS app with the bundle ID below
    4. 
                        
  4. Authentication → Sign-in method → enable Google. This creates the Web client (usually named "Web client (auto created by Google Service)")
    5. 
                        
  5. Download google-services.json and GoogleService-Info.plist again after adding fingerprints, and drop them below — the wizard reads the client IDs from them
    6. 
                    

                

                

                    Open Google Cloud → OAuth clients
                    
    
                        
  1. Configure the consent screen (Google Auth Platform → Branding) if asked
    2. 
                        
  2. Create client → Android: package name + one SHA-1. Create one Android client per SHA-1 below
    3. 
                        
  3. Create client → iOS: bundle ID below → copy its client ID
    4. 
                        
  4. Create client → Web application → copy its client ID (this is the serverClientId)
    5. 
                        
  5. Changes can take from five minutes to a few hours to apply
    6.

 GitHub Secrets

            

                🎯 Goal of this step: register the files that must not be committed as GitHub Secrets, so CI can recreate them. Values never leave this browser — copy them one by one.
            

            

                
                
            

            🔐 Open the repository's Actions secrets page
            
Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → New repository secret. Name = the left column, Secret = the copied value.


            

                

                    
                        

                            Secret name
                            Value
                            Used by
                            Copy
                        

                    
                    
                

            

            
JSON and plist files are stored as raw text (not base64), the same way the existing GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON secret works: CI writes the value back byte for byte, so the format cannot break. Use base64 only for binary files (the extra secrets below convert them automatically).


            

                

                    
➕ Extra secrets (optional)

                    
                

                
Any other file your build needs. Text files stay as they are; binary files become base64.

                

            


            

                
📥 Keep a copy (delete it after registering — it contains secret values)

                

                    
                    
                    
                

            

            

                
                
            

        


        
        
        
        

            
 CI/CD workflows

            

                🎯 Goal of this step: make every build — release, test build and comment-triggered build — produce an app that can log in.
            


            
What each workflow needs

            

                

                    
                        

                            Workflow
                            Change
                        

                    
                    
                

            


            

                

                    
iOS: add this step to two workflows

                    
    
                        
  • .github/workflows/PROJECT-FLUTTER-IOS-TESTFLIGHT.yaml → job build-upload-ios
    • 
                        
  • .github/workflows/PROJECT-FLUTTER-IOS-TEST-TESTFLIGHT.yaml → job build-upload-ios-test
    • 
                    

                    
Where: right after "Ensure .env file exists", before "Set up Flutter" (the job already runs inside your Flutter folder)

                    

                    
The step (indentation matches the other steps)

                    

                    
                    

                        Prefer cat << EOF? Equivalent form
                        
Both write the whole file from the secret. The step above is recommended: the value goes through an environment variable, so no character in the file ($, backticks, a line that reads EOF) can change the script. In the heredoc form the quoted 'EOF' stops the shell from expanding $; it breaks only if the file contains a line EOF.

                        

                        
                    

                    
The plist must also be part of the Runner target once: in Xcode drag GoogleService-Info.plist into Runner (target Runner checked) and commit project.pbxproj. The file itself stays out of Git.

                

                

                    
Android: nothing to add — the step already exists

                    

                    
⚠️ ANDROID-PLAYSTORE-CICD, ANDROID-FIREBASE-CICD and ANDROID-SELFHOSTED-CICD write this file on every build, even when the secret is empty. Register GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON even if you commit the file, or the build overwrites it with an empty one.

                

            

            

                
✅ No workflow file needs a change

                
Your OAuth values live in committed files (AndroidManifest.xml, Info.plist, Dart code), so every workflow builds them as is. What can still break a CI build is a missing key fingerprint — see below.

            

            

                
Comment-triggered builds (@projectops build app / apk build / ios build)

                
PROJECTOPS-APP-BUILD-TRIGGER only dispatches ANDROID-TEST-APK and IOS-TEST-TESTFLIGHT, so it needs no change. But dispatched workflows run the definition on the default branch: merge the iOS step to main before testing it with @projectops ios build, or the old definition runs.

            

            

                
Signing keys used by CI (register their fingerprints)

                
    
                    
  • ANDROID-TEST-APK and ANDROID-FIREBASE-CICD sign with the upload key → upload key SHA-1 / key hash
    • 
                    
  • Builds installed from Google Play are re-signed → Play App Signing SHA-1 / key hash
    • 
                    
  • ANDROID-SELFHOSTED-CICD signs with the DEBUG_KEYSTORE secret by default → run the fingerprint command on that keystore too
    • 
                    
  • iOS needs no fingerprint: Kakao and Google match the bundle ID
    •
